title: Private deploy: cert-rotation cascade disconnect — remediation & action items
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: On 2026-03-09 22:14 UTC a failed certificate rotation in the private control plane caused a cascading disconnect of customer private agents in several VPC deployments. This resulted in transient 5–15 minute API unavailability for management operations (agent heartbeats, configuration fetch) for ~12 customers across multiple regions. No customer data loss was detected; inference traffic continued for pinned model shards but new control-plane commands (rollouts, config changes) were delayed.

Why this ticket: This Linear issue captures the post-incident remediation plan, ownership of long‑term fixes, and tracking of follow-up action items required to prevent recurrence and to harden certificate rotation and agent reconnection behavior in private/VPC deployments.
timeline:
2026-03-09 22:14 UTC - automated cert rotation job started on private control plane nodes
2026-03-09 22:15 UTC - rotation script failed on 3 of 9 control plane nodes due to race condition when updating the wireguard TLS store
2026-03-09 22:16 UTC - healthcheck loop observed certificate mismatch; outbound connections to agent tunnels were rejected
2026-03-09 22:18 UTC - control plane leader re-election triggered; small window where control plane API responded slowly
2026-03-09 22:25 UTC - mitigation: rollback of rotated certs to previous version and restart of control plane components completed
2026-03-09 22:30 UTC - agent reconnection observed and normal operations recovered
2026-03-10 09:00 UTC - incident declared for follow-up and root cause analysis
root_cause: A race condition in the certificate rotation orchestration caused partial writes to the wireguard/agent TLS key store on a subset of control plane nodes. When the leader updated and began serving new certs while followers still had old cert metadata, agent mutual TLS checks failed, causing connections to be rejected. The rotation job lacked a quorum-safe barrier and sufficient preflight validation for active connections. Additionally, agent retry/backoff windows were such that short-lived control plane instability led to multiple reconnection failures before exponential backoff allowed recovery.
mitigation_taken: Immediate rollback of certificates to the last-known-good set and restart of control plane components. Temporarily disabled the automated rotation job across private control planes until a safe, quorum-aware rotation path is implemented. Notified affected customers and opened support tickets; provided manual guidance for customers running on tightly-coupled on-prem proxies.
action_items: AI-1: Implement quorum-aware certificate rotation orchestration that applies new certs only after a two-phase commit across control-plane nodes. Owner: Marcus Chen. Due: 2026-03-20. Status: In Progress.

AI-2: Add a pre-rotation connectivity probe that validates agent mutual-TLS acceptance on a canary subset before committing rotation cluster-wide. Owner: Elena Ruiz. Due: 2026-03-18. Status: In Progress.

AI-3: Harden agent reconnection logic to support aggressive short-term retries with jitter for the first 60s after control-plane leader changes. Owner: Daniel Kim. Due: 2026-03-22. Estimate: 5. Status: Planned.

AI-4: Add runbook steps and automated playbook for safe rollback of cert rotations, including dashboard playbook links and Slack automations. Owner: Priya Sharma (SRE). Due: 2026-03-15. Status: In Progress.

AI-5: Create an integration test that simulates partial rotation (N-1 nodes) and validates agent behavior and leader election safety. Owner: Marcus Chen. Due: 2026-03-24. Estimate: 3. Status: Backlog.
AI-6: Add alerting for asymmetric cert versions across control-plane nodes (threshold: >30% divergence) and surface to oncall immediately. Owner: SRE team. Due: 2026-03-16. Status: In Progress.

AI-7: Customer communication follow-up: compile incident impact summary and mitigation guidance for affected private customers; include guidance for on-prem network appliances that inspect TLS sessions. Owner: Aisha Patel (PM). Due: 2026-03-14. Status: Done.

notes: This incident highlights a class of failures where control-plane choreography and client-side reconnection policies interact badly. Longer-term roadmap consideration: support zero-downtime certificate rolling via out-of-band sidecar certs for agents. Add to private deployment roadmap Q2 2026.
